supportTiers.Full: A packed-NuGet consumer publishes and executes as Native AOT without TCJ-caused trimming or AOT warnings for the supported usage path.
supportTiers.Conditional: The package is supported only through explicitly documented safe paths or while respecting named upstream restrictions.
supportTiers.Experimental: The package may be exercised with Native AOT, but TCJ does not make a production-support promise for that path.
supportTiers.Unsupported: TCJ does not support Native AOT consumption for the package or usage path.

packages.rationale: TCJ.Core is Full for the supported package-consumer path. The release gate consumes the locally packed TCJ.Core package, publishes the linux-x64 smoke application with PublishAot=true, executes the native binary, verifies the loaded assembly PackageVersion metadata, and rejects any IL2xxx/IL3xxx diagnostics.

TCJ.DependencyInjection is Full for the explicit Native AOT-safe path: AddTcjDependencyInjection(), AddTcjDomainEvent<TEvent>(), and explicit Microsoft DI handler/service registration. The linux-x64 packed-package smoke publishes and executes that path and validates the loaded package version. Reflection-based convention scanning remains individually restricted and is not part of the Full path.

restrictions.reason: This overload invokes Assembly.GetTypes()-based convention scanning and enables runtime generic domain-event dispatch. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode. Native AOT/trimming consumers must use the parameterless bootstrap, AddTcjDomainEvent<TEvent>(), and explicit registrations.

This scanner-capable overload can select reflection-based assembly discovery and the runtime generic dispatch fallback. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode. Use the explicit registration path for Native AOT/trimming.

This scanner-capable overload enumerates consumer assemblies through runtime reflection and enables the runtime generic dispatch fallback. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode. Use the explicit registration path for Native AOT/trimming.
These APIs opt callers into convention scanning. They are only consumed by the scanner-capable AddTcjDependencyInjection overloads, which surface the trimming and Native AOT restrictions.

packages.rationale: TCJ exercises a project-reference EF Core NativeAOT fixture with EF compiled-model and query-precompilation tooling, and trims TCJ-owned runtime Type usage from the static model-convention/serialization path where practical. The package remains Experimental because EF Core NativeAOT is upstream-experimental and TCJ retains explicitly restricted runtime-discovery APIs.

restrictions.symbol: Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore NativeAOT compiled models and precompiled queries
restrictions.reason: EF Core NativeAOT and query precompilation are upstream-experimental. NativeAOT consumers require EF publish tooling that generates a compiled model and precompiled queries; dynamic queries, query-expression syntax, captured-state value converters, and some provider scenarios remain limited. EF compiled models also do not support global query filters, lazy-loading/change-tracking proxies, or custom IModelCacheKeyFactory implementations.

The API scans arbitrary assemblies and closes generic ApplyConfiguration methods from runtime Type values. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode; NativeAOT consumers must configure the model explicitly before EF compiled-model generation.

The API discovers entity types with Assembly.GetExportedTypes() and registers runtime Type values. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode; NativeAOT consumers must register entity types explicitly.
The API discovers loaded module assemblies at runtime. It is annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and is excluded from the experimental NativeAOT fixture.

The TCJ soft-delete convention installs EF global query filters. EF compiled models required by the current NativeAOT path do not support global query filters, so this convention is outside the experimental NativeAOT path while normal JIT usage remains supported.

Entity search builds predicates and closes generic executor types from runtime EF model metadata. The contract and implementation are annotated with RequiresUnreferencedCode and RequiresDynamicCode; NativeAOT consumers should use statically typed repository/DbContext queries that EF tooling can precompile.

The default event resolver can scan loaded assemblies when a persisted convention event name is not explicitly registered. NativeAOT experiments must register persisted event contracts with AddTcjOutboxEvent<TEvent> and provide System.Text.Json metadata for event payload types; the Important 7 fixture intentionally does not claim the outbox path.

The fixture is project-reference evidence only. It requires PublishAot, a concrete RID, Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Tasks, EFOptimizeContext for EF Core 10, generated-interceptor opt-in, and publish-stage compiled-model/query precompilation. It does not qualify as packed-package production support evidence.

packages.rationale: The SQL Server provider path is exercised by the same project-reference EF NativeAOT fixture and TCJ rowversion conventions avoid runtime Entity(Type) configuration, but support remains Experimental because EF provider participation and NativeAOT query precompilation are upstream-experimental and there is no packed-consumer production evidence.

restrictions.reason: EF Core NativeAOT is upstream-experimental and providers participate in precompiled-query support. The provider path also inherits the provider-neutral compiled-model limitations documented for TCJ.EntityFrameworkCore, including the global-query-filter boundary. TCJ therefore makes no Full or production-ready claim for SQL Server NativeAOT.

The fixture configures SQL Server, generates the compiled model and precompiled queries during linux-x64 NativeAOT publish, and executes without contacting a database. It is project-reference experiment evidence, not a packaged provider guarantee.

packages.rationale: TCJ.AspNetCore is Full for the documented ASP.NET Core Native AOT Minimal API path. The linux-x64 release gate consumes the packed Core, DependencyInjection, and AspNetCore packages, publishes with PublishAot=true, starts the native host, verifies representative HTTP/error behavior and explicit domain-event dispatch, checks loaded package versions, and rejects new IL2xxx/IL3xxx diagnostics. Upstream-unsupported ASP.NET Core feature families remain outside this support path.

restrictions.symbol: ASP.NET Core Native AOT feature compatibility matrix for net10.0
restrictions.reason: TCJ.AspNetCore supports Native AOT only inside upstream-supported ASP.NET Core feature families. The verified TCJ path uses Minimal APIs and framework-native Problem Details/current-user/health primitives. MVC controllers, Blazor Server, SignalR, and other upstream-unsupported feature families are not made AOT-compatible by TCJ.
